title: Private Deploy: Minimal-Trust Bootstrap, Egress Consent & Upgrade Acceptance Criteria
creator: Sofia Kim
description: This PRD defines requirements and acceptance criteria for a minimal-trust bootstrap flow and explicit egress consent model for Private/VPC deployments. Goal: allow customers to run Redwood Private in constrained networks (partial or zero egress) while preserving safe upgrade paths, signed artifact provenance, and optional telemetry consents. This covers networking constraints, offline/air-gapped upgrade options, operator handshake, and runbook-level rollback criteria.
decisions: Adopt minimal-trust bootstrap: operator will perform a cryptographic handshake against a pre-provisioned signing key rather than relying on continuous outbound control-plane connections.
Default behavior: require explicit customer opt-in for any telemetry; minimal liveness telemetry allowed for health checks only and must be disabled by default in zero-egress profiles.
Upgrade orchestration will support two modes: staged online canary (preferred) and signed-offline bundle (airgap). Both must satisfy artifact signature verification before install.
Image signing: use existing image signing format (cosign-compatible) and verify using customer-supplied root key or Redwood-provided key when customer permits.
Rollback triggers: automatic rollback if operator detects >5% pod failure rate within 15 minutes of new version rollout or if KMS rotation fails to validate.
acceptance_criteria: Network: Private control-plane calls are optional. Customer can choose 'zero-egress' profile; in this profile the operator must complete bootstrap using only local artifacts or signed mirror endpoints.

Bootstrap: Operator can bootstrap cluster from a signed bundle delivered via S3-like mirror, HTTP mirror, or physical media. Successful bootstrap includes verification of signatures and manifest checksum.

Upgrade: For airgapped upgrades, the on-disk operator must accept a signed upgrade bundle and produce a deterministic preflight report verifying node compatibility and disk space; preflight report must be stored locally and human-readable.

Telemetry & Consent: Default settings must disable non-essential telemetry. If telemetry is enabled, operator will present a consent manifest and will not transmit data until customer toggles consent. Consent must be revocable.

KMS / Key Management: KMS integration must support customer-managed keys. During upgrades that require key material rotation, operator will simulate rotation in dry-run and produce a rollback-safe plan before committing.

Image provenance: All images and operator binaries used in bootstrap/upgrade must be checked against a signed provenance manifest. Any mismatch blocks rollout and surfaces a clear error with remediation steps.
SLOs: In zero-egress and minimal-trust modes the operator must not increase median pod startup time by more than 15% compared to hosted baseline for common cluster sizes (<=20 nodes).
Observability: When telemetry is disabled, operator will expose a local read-only trace/log bundle that customers can collect; no external endpoints are contacted.

Operator safety: New operator release must provide a dry-run execution path and an automatic rollback capability that reverts to last-known-good operator state without requiring external connectivity.
Documentation: Runbook and upgrade checklist must be published in Confluence and linked from the operator UI prior to GA.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers with strict airgap may misapply unsigned bundles -> Mitigation: operator refuses to apply unsigned or improperly-signed bundles in default policy; provide explicit --allow-unsigned for advanced ops with warnings.

Risk: KMS rotation failure during offline upgrade causing data unavailability -> Mitigation: require dry-run rotation and a fallback key stored in k8s sealed secret accessible only to operator rollback path.
Risk: Telemetry opt-in accidentally enabled -> Mitigation: default to disabled; include explicit consent manifest and audit trail of consent toggles in local logs.
Risk: Long upgrade windows for large clusters with no egress -> Mitigation: support staged rollouts by node-label groups and provide estimated completion times in preflight.
Risk: Customer operator misconfiguration -> Mitigation: provide validation tooling (local sanity checks) and preflight report with actionable remediation steps.
Risk: Signed artifact key compromise -> Mitigation: support key rotation and revocation lists; document emergency rollback and manual verification steps.
Risk: Performance regressions in minimal-trust path -> Mitigation: benchmark scripts and regression alerts (console-2025.03) tied to token-level cost/latency dashboards.
open_questions: Should we allow Redwood-hosted mirror endpoints as a convenience for customers that enable egress? (security team leaning towards opt-in only.)
What is the maximum allowed size for signed offline bundles before we require chunked delivery?
Do we require operator to ship an embedded list of default root keys for small customers, or always require customer-supplied root-of-trust?
How should we surface consent revocation in the Console UI for Private customers?
What audit log retention do customers expect for telemetry consent events in closed networks?
updates: 2025-01-12: Initial scoping session with Security and Infra; agreed minimal-trust approach as default for zero-egress.
2025-01-20: Draft PRD circulated to Solutions Eng; requested explicit runbook artifacts and preflight schema.
2025-01-28: Infra proposed cosign-compatible signing; Security approved with additional key-rotation constraints.
2025-02-03: UX provided consent manifest mockups; added requirement for revocable consent and audit trail.
2025-02-05: RFC posted to #private-deployments; awaiting ENG-4021 implementation estimate for dry-run rotation.
Review feedback: Elena Park (Security) asked to add emergency manual verification flow; Miguel Duarte (Infra) requested clearer chunking guidance for large bundles.
test_plan: TP-001: Offline bootstrap from signed tarball via local mirror -> passes signature verification, completes install.
TP-002: Attempt bootstrap with unsigned bundle -> operator blocks install and emits remediation steps.
TP-003: Airgap upgrade dry-run key-rotation -> dry-run completes with no changes and produces rollback plan.
TP-004: Telemetry disabled profile -> network capture shows zero outbound telemetry endpoints called during normal operations.
TP-005: Canary rollback -> simulate 10% of nodes failing to start after new operator; automated rollback reverts within SLAs.
TP-006: Consent revocation -> toggling consent off prevents future telemetry and logs audit event locally.
TP-007: Preflight for cluster with <10% disk free -> preflight fails with clear remediation steps and blocks upgrade.
TP-008: Performance regression test -> minimal-trust path median startup within 15% of baseline.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood in Redwood private lab clusters, exercise all test_plan cases.
Phase 1: Invite-only pilot with 3 customers who require minimal egress; collect feedback and telemetry consent patterns.
Phase 2: Broader private rollout with opt-in mirrors and documentation; enable console guidance for offline bundle preparation.
Phase 3: GA with runbooks, signed operator bundles, and public Confluence docs.
rollback_criteria: Automatic: >5% pod crashloop or >10% request error rate in 15 minutes post-rollout triggers rollback.
Manual: Failed key verification during post-upgrade checks or missing preflight artifacts -> immediate manual rollback required.
Operator-level: If dry-run rotation differs from actual rotation plan outputs, abort upgrade and revert to previous operator image.
